collections.summary: Know which array methods mutate and which copy, how holes, sorting and reduce behave at the edges, and when a Map, Set or weak collection beats a plain object or array.
points: Mutators: push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, sort, reverse, fill, copyWithin. Copying versions (ES2023): toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced, with.
`sort()` compares strings by default, so pass `(a, b) => a - b` for numbers. Comparators must return negative, zero or positive consistently. Sort is stable since ES2019.
Always give `reduce` an initial value: it avoids the empty-array TypeError and the single-element shortcut.
Destructuring defaults apply only to `undefined`. Object rest and spread copy own enumerable properties into a new plain object and are shallow.
Map keeps key types and pure insertion order and has `size`. Set dedupes with SameValueZero (NaN equals NaN, -0 becomes +0). ES2025 adds union, intersection and friends.
WeakMap and WeakSet hold object (or non-registered symbol) keys weakly and can't be iterated. WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry give no timing guarantees.
Array-likes have `length`; iterables have `Symbol.iterator`. Array.from accepts both, spread only iterables.
traps: `['1', '2', '3'].map(parseInt)` is `[1, NaN, NaN]` because map passes the index as the radix.
Holes: forEach, map, filter and indexOf skip them; for...of, Array.from, includes and toSorted read them as undefined.
`Object.groupBy` returns a null-prototype object, not a Map, so `result.hasOwnProperty` is undefined.
